backlog.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.descList (about 210 values, e.g. MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt) as features, concatenated with the Morgan bits. Replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RF.
backlog.title: RDKit descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Replace the RF with LightGBM (n_estimators 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample_bytree 0.5, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on RDKit descriptors only. Sanitize NaN/inf.
backlog.title: Descriptors only with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with radius 2, 2048 bits so that features are substructure counts. Keep the RF.
backlog.title: Morgan counts instead of bits

backlog.spec: Features: Morgan count FP (radius 2, 2048) plus RDKit descriptors. Model: LightGBM with 1000 trees, lr 0.03, colsample 0.3, num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 10, L1 objective.
backlog.title: Count Morgan + descriptors in LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor (iterations 1500, depth 6, lr 0.05, loss MAE or RMSE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed) on RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts at 1024 bits. Check the time stays under the 10 min limit.
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors+counts

backlog.spec: Train the GBM with Huber loss (alpha about 1.0) or L1 objective, since the metric is MAE. Base on LightGBM with descriptors and Morgan counts.
backlog.title: MAE/Huber objective

backlog.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the existing Morgan features and keep the RF.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Add count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator (fpSize 1024) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator (fpSize 1024) to the Morgan features. Keep the RF.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count FPs

backlog.spec: Add per-molecule features based on Crippen: the sum of logP contributions per atom type (rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs grouped by atom environment) or simply MolLogP and MolMR with TPSA, HBD and HBA counts. Add them to the Morgan bits in the RF.
backlog.title: Crippen atom contributions

backlog.spec: Fit RF, LightGBM and CatBoost on the same descriptor+count features. Return the mean of the three predictions. Keep each model modest so the total runtime stays below 8 min.
backlog.title: Ensemble RF+LGBM+CatBoost average

backlog.spec: Replace the RF with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, n_jobs -1) on Morgan counts plus descriptors.
backlog.title: Extra Trees

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto/MinMax kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048) between molecules. Fit sklearn SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train kernel, predict with the test-train kernel.
backlog.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed MinMax kernel on Morgan counts (alpha 0.5). Center y by subtracting the train mean and add it back at prediction.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto

backlog.spec: Implement GP regression with numpy: K = Tanimoto kernel on count FPs, noise 0.3. Solve (K+σ²I)α = y−mean with scipy.linalg.cho_solve. Predict with K*α.
backlog.title: Gaussian process Tanimoto

backlog.spec: Set RADIUS 3 and N_BITS 4096 with count FPs. Use LightGBM or RF with colsample 0.2.
backlog.title: Larger radius Morgan with features

backlog.spec: Add FCFP-like fingerprints via GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()) counts at 1024 bits, concatenated with ECFP counts.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP)

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF 2, MAX_FEATURES 0.2, N_TREES 500 for the RF, with descriptors added.
backlog.title: RF hyperparameter tuning

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor (hist, n_estimators 800, lr 0.03, max_depth 6, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.4, reg_lambda 2, objective reg:pseudohubererror or squarederror, n_jobs 8) on descriptors+Morgan counts.
backlog.title: XGBoost on descriptors+counts

backlog.spec: Average 5 LightGBM models with different seeds derived from seed, each with subsample 0.7 and colsample 0.4, on descriptors+counts.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM

backlog.spec: LightGBM with lambda_l2 10, min_child_samples 20, max_depth 6, num_leaves 24, learning_rate 0.02, 1500 trees with early stopping on an inner 10 percent validation split (seeded), then predict.
backlog.title: Stronger GBM regularization

backlog.spec: Standardize descriptors (QuantileTransformer to normal), and fit sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden 512,256, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping). Average 5 seeds and blend 50/50 with an RF on the Morgan+descriptor features.
backlog.title: MLP on descriptors

backlog.spec: Average the predictions of LightGBM on descriptors+counts and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR on counts, weights 0.5 each.
backlog.title: Stack of GBM and Tanimoto SVR

backlog.spec: Drop training molecules whose y lies beyond 3 SD from the train mean, or whose RF out-of-fold residual is over 2.5. Then fit the final model on the rest.
backlog.title: Remove outlier targets

backlog.spec: Drop features with fewer than 5 nonzero molecules in the training set (Morgan bits) and constant descriptors before fitting. Fit the RF or LightGBM on the remaining ones.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance

backlog.spec: Add SMARTS counts for acids (carboxylic, sulfonic, tetrazole), basic amines (aliphatic, amidine, guanidine), quaternary N and phenols, plus formal charge. Append to descriptors and Morgan counts; this helps logD at pH 7.4.
backlog.title: Ionization/functional group counts

backlog.spec: Before featurization, take the largest fragment with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser and neutralize with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Keep the RF with Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules

backlog.spec: Fit a linear model of y on MolLogP and TPSA, then fit LightGBM on the residuals using descriptors and counts. Prediction is linear plus GBM.
backlog.title: Residual stacking on Crippen logP

backlog.spec: Train separate LightGBM models on Morgan counts, atom-pair counts and descriptors. Average the three predictions.
backlog.title: Ensemble of different FP models

backlog.spec: Weight train samples by 1/sqrt of the Murcko scaffold group size so large analog series do not dominate the fit. Pass sample_weight to the LightGBM fit on descriptors+counts.
backlog.title: Sample-weight by scaffold rarity

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, train 5 LGBMRegressor models with identical params but random_state=seed+i (i=0..4) and different subsample/colsample draws, and return the mean of their predictions. Compute features once. Keep n_jobs=8. This reduces variance without changing the feature set.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM

backlog.spec: In featurize, append hashed count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=1024) (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) to the existing Morgan counts and descriptors. Leave the LightGBM settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add features: per-atom Crippen logP and MR contributions summed into bins by contribution type (rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs, using the 68 atom type labels from Crippen's tables via the logP contribution values), plus the EState fingerprint counts (rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol, concatenated counts and sums). Append them to the current feature matrix.
backlog.title: Crippen/EState per-atom contribution features

backlog.spec: Compute Crippen MolLogP for train and test molecules. Fit a linear regression of y on MolLogP on the training set, then train LightGBM on the residuals y - linear_pred (same features). Predict as linear_pred + gbm_pred. This gives the trees a physics-based baseline.
backlog.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP

backlog.spec: Change LGBMRegressor to n_estimators=3000, learning_rate=0.01, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_samples=15, reg_lambda=5, subsample=0.7, and keep the objective. Check that the time stays under 10 minutes. If it is too slow, use 2000 trees at lr 0.015.
backlog.title: Larger LightGBM with lower learning rate and strong regularization

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM objective from l1 to huber with alpha=0.8 (the Huber delta in target units) and keep everything else the same. L1 gives weak gradients for trees. Huber may fit the bulk better while staying robust to outliers.
backlog.title: Huber objective

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training set for (a) the current LightGBM and (b) an SVR (C=5) on a Tanimoto kernel of Morgan counts (min/max kernel). Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn LinearRegression positive=True) on the two OOF columns. Refit both on all training data and combine for the test set using the learned weights. Use GroupKFold-free plain KFold with the seed.
backlog.title: Stack LightGBM with Tanimoto SVR using inner CV

backlog.spec: Add a torch-free sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers 512,256, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=300) trained on QuantileTransformer(normal)-scaled RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts reduced with log1p. Average 3 seeds. Blend 0.7*LightGBM + 0.3*MLP. Report the predictions blended.
backlog.title: MLP on standardized descriptors ensemble member

backlog.spec: After featurize, compute the variance on the training matrix and drop columns with fewer than 5 nonzero training molecules, then drop descriptor columns with absolute Pearson correlation greater than 0.95 to an earlier column. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Train the same LightGBM on the reduced set, so colsample is spent on useful columns.
backlog.title: Drop near-constant and correlated features

backlog.spec: In featurize, standardize each molecule with rdMolStandardize: LargestFragmentChooser, then Uncharger, before computing the fingerprints and descriptors. Fall back to the original molecule if standardization fails. This removes salt and charge artifacts that distort logD descriptors.
backlog.title: Neutralize and take the largest fragment before featurization

backlog.spec: Fit a Ridge/linear regression of y on Crippen MolLogP (Descriptors.MolLogP, already column in desc) using training data only, subtract its prediction from y, train XGBoost on the residual and add the linear prediction back to the XGBoost output only (the MLP half stays on raw y). This repeats slot 16 (0.4985) to check whether the gain is real; keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Replicate Crippen residual for XGBoost half

backlog.spec: Change the XGBoost huber_slope from 1.0 to 0.6 and base_score to the median of y (base_score=float(np.median(y))). Leave all else unchanged. Smaller slope makes the loss closer to MAE, the scoring metric, and the median base score helps pseudohuber converge.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber slope tuning

backlog.spec: Extend the MLP inputs: besides the quantile-transformed descriptor block, add the top 128 components of TruncatedSVD (random_state=seed) fit on the Morgan count block (log1p of counts) of the training set, standardized. Feed the concatenation to the 5 MLPs. XGBoost unchanged.
backlog.title: MLP on descriptors plus Morgan SVD

backlog.spec: Change MLPRegressor to hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-1, and raise the seed count from 5 to 8, with learning_rate_init=5e-4. Stronger weight decay on small data with a quantile-transformed input may reduce overfitting to training scaffolds.
backlog.title: MLP weight-decay and dropout-like regularization sweep

backlog.spec: Change the final blend from 0.5/0.5 to 0.4*p_tree + 0.6*p_mlp. The MLP ensemble may be the stronger member; this tests asymmetric weighting.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.4 tree / 0.6 MLP

backlog.spec: Compute a MinMax (Tanimoto) kernel on Morgan count columns (first N_BITS columns) between train/train and test/train, fit sklearn SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on y minus mean, add the mean back, and blend as 0.4 XGB + 0.4 MLP + 0.2 SVR. A different inductive bias for scaffold-split generalization.
backlog.title: Add a Tanimoto-kernel SVR as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) for each training molecule and pass sample_weight=1/sqrt(count of molecules sharing that scaffold) normalized to mean 1 to XGBoost fit. This downweights over-represented scaffolds so the model focuses on skeleton diversity, matching the scaffold-split evaluation.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights

backlog.spec: Set XGBoost max_depth=4, n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.02, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.7. Shallower trees with stronger regularization may generalize better to unseen scaffolds. Check that runtime stays under limit.
backlog.title: Shallower, more regularized XGBoost

backlog.spec: In featurize, before computing features, use rdMolStandardize: take the LargestFragmentChooser fragment and apply Uncharger (neutralize) to each molecule, falling back to the original molecule on exception. Ion SMARTS counts and formal charge would then be computed on the standardized molecule, but compute formal charge from the original molecule so charge info is retained.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurization

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute 5-fold out-of-fold MLP predictions on the training set (KFold, shuffle, seed; 3 MLPs per fold for speed) and append them as one extra feature column to XGBoost's Xtr; for Xte use the MLP ensemble fit on all training data. Final prediction is 0.7*XGBoost-with-stack + 0.3*p_mlp. Tests stacking instead of plain averaging. Watch runtime (<10 min total).
backlog.title: Quantile-transformed descriptors added to XGBoost via a stacked MLP prediction

backlog.spec: In fit_predict change the final return to 0.4 * p_tree + 0.6 * p_mlp. No other change. Tests whether the MLP half deserves more weight.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.4 tree / 0.6 MLP

backlog.spec: In the MLPRegressor ensemble change alpha from 1e-2 to 1e-1 and hidden_layer_sizes to (1024, 256). Keep 5 seeds and early stopping. Tests stronger L2 regularization on the neural half.
backlog.title: MLP weight decay and width sweep point

backlog.spec: Add TruncatedSVD (128 components, random_state=seed) fit on the training Morgan count columns (first N_BITS columns of Xtr, apply log1p first). Standardize the SVD output with the QuantileTransformer and concatenate to the descriptor input Dtr/Dte for the MLPs only. XGBoost is unchanged.
backlog.title: MLP with Morgan SVD features

backlog.spec: In featurize, before computing features, standardize each molecule with rdMolStandardize: take LargestFragmentChooser and then Uncharger. Fall back to the original mol if it fails. Keep the formal charge feature computed from the original molecule so ionization info is retained.
backlog.title: Neutralize and take largest fragment

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and its group size. Pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(group size), normalized to mean 1, to XGBRegressor.fit. This reduces the dominance of large scaffold families and may help generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Train a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function='MAE', iterations 1500, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, thread_count 8, random_seed=seed, verbose=0) on the descriptors plus ionization columns only, without Morgan bits. Blend as 0.4 XGBoost + 0.4 MLP + 0.2 CatBoost.
backlog.title: Add a CatBoost member with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Increase the MLP ensemble to 10 seeds with hidden_layer_sizes (512,256) and learning_rate_init 5e-4, n_iter_no_change 20. Averaging more seeds reduces variance in the neural half. Check that runtime stays under the 10 minute limit.
backlog.title: MLP with MAE-friendly target and larger ensemble

backlog.spec: Compute predictions from the XGBoost model and each of the 5 MLPs separately. Final prediction = 0.5 * p_tree + 0.5 * the median across the 5 MLP predictions, instead of the mean. This gives robustness to outlier MLP members.
backlog.title: Median blend instead of mean

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBoost fit with 1600 trees at learning_rate 0.015 and add a LearningRateScheduler callback using xgboost.callback.LearningRateScheduler with a cosine decay from 0.04 to 0.002 across the rounds. Keep other parameters.
backlog.title: Cosine-style learning rate decay for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace the np.mean over the 5 MLP seeds with np.median across the 5 predictions (axis=0), keeping the 50/50 blend with XGBoost. This reduces the effect of a bad MLP seed.
backlog.title: Median blend of MLP members

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule with rdkit MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles. Weight each molecule by 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in the training set), normalized to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to XGBRegressor.fit. Leave the MLP unchanged, since MLPRegressor takes no weights. This should help generalization to unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Before featurization, in featurize, take the largest fragment of each molecule with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser and neutralize it with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Wrap the step in try/except and fall back to the original molecule. Then compute all features from the cleaned mol. Salts and charge states may otherwise add noise.
backlog.title: Standardize and neutralize molecules

backlog.spec: For each of 5 MLPs, train on a random 70% subset of the quantile-transformed descriptor columns, chosen with np.random.RandomState(seed+k). Raise the ensemble to 8 nets. Average the predictions. This adds diversity, like a random subspace ensemble.
backlog.title: Drop-out style MLP via per-net feature subsampling

backlog.spec: Train each MLP on a bootstrap resample of the training rows, drawn with RandomState(seed+k), instead of the full set. Use 8 nets. Average the predictions. Bagging adds variance diversity to the MLP half.
backlog.title: Bagged MLPs on bootstrap samples

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member: an MLPRegressor (256,128), alpha 1e-1, early_stopping, trained on log1p of the Morgan counts, columns with at least 10 nonzero training molecules, concatenated with the quantile-transformed descriptors. Use 3 seeds. Blend 0.4 XGBoost, 0.3 descriptor MLP, 0.3 this MLP.
backlog.title: Add a Morgan-count MLP member

backlog.spec: Fit the MLP ensemble first. Then fit XGBoost on y minus the MLP's prediction on the training data. Instead of in-sample predictions, use the MLP early-stopping out-of-sample behaviour: shrink the MLP prediction by 0.5 before subtracting, which limits leakage. Final prediction is p_mlp + p_xgb_resid. This is sequential boosting on top of the neural net, in place of a parallel blend.
backlog.title: Target transform: fit on residual from MLP ensemble

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, drop training molecules whose y is more than 3.0 median absolute deviations (scaled by 1.4826) from the median of y. Fit both XGBoost and MLP on the remaining rows. Test predictions are unaffected. This reduces the influence of noisy labels.
backlog.title: Remove extreme-target outliers from training

backlog.spec: Before featurization, standardize each molecule: keep the largest fragment (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, pick the one with most heavy atoms) and neutralize charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger().uncharge. Fall back to the original molecule if anything fails. Compute the formal charge and quaternary N SMARTS feature on the original molecule so ionization info is kept, and compute fingerprints and descriptors on the standardized one. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Neutralize and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Change the final blend weights from 0.4 XGB / 0.3 descriptor MLP / 0.3 fingerprint MLP to 0.3 / 0.35 / 0.35. Change nothing else. This is a single-point check that the MLP members deserve more weight.
backlog.title: Blend weight retune

backlog.spec: Replace the weighted mean of the three members with the median of the three predictions, taken per molecule with np.median over a stacked array. Change nothing else. This should reduce the damage when one member is wrong on an unseen scaffold.
backlog.title: Median blend of members

backlog.spec: For the descriptor MLP and the fingerprint MLP, switch solver to 'adam' with learning_rate_init 2e-3 and a manual snapshot ensemble. Loop 4 times calling partial_fit for 40 epochs each with learning_rate_init halved each cycle. Average the predictions from the end of every cycle. Use a fixed validation-free setup, with no early_stopping. Keep alpha unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine-decayed MLP via SGD restarts

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, fit an out-of-fold-free quick check: train a shallow XGBoost on the training set, compute in-sample residuals, then drop the 1.5% of training molecules with the largest absolute residual from all three members' training sets. Fit the final models on the remaining rows only.
backlog.title: Drop outlier targets

backlog.spec: For the fingerprint MLP member only, build the log1p count input from Morgan radius 1 (1024 bits) concatenated with radius 3 (2048 bits) and the quantile-transformed descriptors. Keep the count>=10 column filter. XGBoost keeps its current inputs.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan MLP input

backlog.spec: Augment the MLP training sets: stack two copies of the training matrix, one clean and one with Gaussian noise (sd 0.1) added to the quantile-transformed descriptor columns. Use the same y for both copies. Apply it to both MLP members, keeping the MLP ensemble sizes. This acts as input-noise regularization.
backlog.title: Target-noise augmentation for MLPs

backlog.spec: Replace the single XGBoost with two models averaged: the current pseudo-Huber one and an otherwise identical one with objective reg:squarederror and max_depth 5, with different random_state. Give the averaged output the same 0.4 blend weight.
backlog.title: Mixed-loss XGBoost pair

backlog.spec: Add a fourth blend member: an MLPRegressor with hidden layers (1024, 512, 128), alpha 0.3, early_stopping True, on the same inputs as the fingerprint MLP, averaged over 3 seeds. Blend weights: 0.35 XGB, 0.2 descriptor MLP, 0.25 fingerprint MLP, 0.2 new MLP.
backlog.title: Wide shallow-residual MLP (bold)

backlog.spec: Append to the descriptor block the rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors values CalcNumAmideBonds, CalcNumHeterocycles, CalcNumSpiroAtoms, CalcNumBridgeheadAtoms, CalcNumAtomStereoCenters, plus the BCUT2D features (rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D) and the topological polar surface area with S and P included (CalcTPSA(m, includeSandP=True)). Wrap in nan_to_num. These go into all three members through the existing descriptor block.
backlog.title: Chirality and 3D-free shape descriptors

backlog.spec: Combine two near-misses. In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize it (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger), falling back to the original mol on error. Then in fit_predict train the existing pseudo-Huber XGBoost and a second XGBRegressor (objective reg:squarederror, max_depth 5, other params same, random_state seed+1) and average them as the tree member p_tree = 0.5*(p1+p2). Keep the 0.4/0.3/0.3 blend.
backlog.title: Neutralize plus second squared-error XGBoost

backlog.spec: Change the final blend from 0.4/0.3/0.3 to 0.3*p_tree + 0.35*p_mlp + 0.35*p_fp. Change nothing else. This tests whether more weight on the two MLP members helps, since they are the stronger diverse members.
backlog.title: Blend weight retune with rank-free grid

backlog.spec: Replace the final weighted mean with a robust combination. Stack p_tree, p_mlp and p_fp as columns and return the median across the three members. Also keep the individual predictions unchanged. The metric is MAE, so the median may reduce the effect of an occasionally bad member.
backlog.title: Median blend of members

backlog.spec: Fit the MLP members on residuals. Compute 5-fold OOF XGBoost predictions on the training set (KFold shuffled with seed, a smaller XGB of 300 trees, lr 0.08 to save time), then train the descriptor MLP on y minus the OOF prediction. Add the full-data XGBoost test prediction back to the MLP residual prediction. Blend this residual model 50/50 with the current final blend. Keep the total runtime under about 8 minutes.
backlog.title: Residual MLP on XGBoost out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Add a learning-rate schedule to the XGBoost member. Use xgboost.callback.LearningRateScheduler with a cosine decay from 0.06 to 0.005 over 800 trees, in the fit/constructor callbacks. Keep the other XGBoost params. This tests schedule effects on the tree member.
backlog.title: Cosine-decay lr schedule via XGBoost callbacks

backlog.spec: Use Crippen MolLogP and TPSA as auxiliary outputs. Train the descriptor MLP with a 3-column target [y, standardized MolLogP, standardized TPSA] via MLPRegressor multi-output, then use only column 0 of the prediction. Do the same for the Morgan-count MLP. Both aux targets are computed from the SMILES with RDKit, so there is no leakage. The aux tasks regularize the hidden layers.
backlog.title: Multi-task auxiliary targets for MLP

backlog.spec: Add a fourth blend member: sklearn Ridge (alpha tuned via RidgeCV over [1,10,100,1000]) on the concatenation of the quantile-transformed descriptors and log1p Morgan columns with at least 10 nonzero counts, plus pairwise squares of the top 30 descriptors by absolute correlation to y. Blend as 0.9*current blend + 0.1*ridge. This adds a low-variance linear member.
backlog.title: Wide shallow bagged-feature ridge member

backlog.spec: For the Morgan-count and descriptor features, the result is invariant to atom order, so use a different augmentation. Augment training by adding Gaussian jitter (sd 0.05 in quantile-normal space) to the descriptor columns for 2 extra copies of the training set in the descriptor MLP only, keeping y unchanged. Average 5 MLP seeds as before. Keep the test inputs unaltered.
backlog.title: Test-time augmentation by randomized SMILES atom order

backlog.spec: Clip the training targets for the two MLP members only to the 1st and 99th percentiles of y, leaving XGBoost on the raw y. This reduces the influence of extreme logD values on squared-loss MLPs, which matters for the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Huber-style MLP via target winsorizing

backlog.spec: Add fragment-count descriptors. Append all rdkit.Chem.Fragments fr_* counts (already in descList, so instead add) the per-molecule counts of ring sizes (3 to 8), number of aromatic rings by heteroatom content, and BCUT2D descriptors (rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D) plus the MQN descriptors (rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_). Append to the descriptor block so both the XGBoost and the MLPs see them.
backlog.title: Add Morgan radius-3 count-sum pooled features and ring/fragment counts

backlog.spec: Combine two near-misses. At the start of fit_predict, standardize each SMILES: parse, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), then neutralize with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. If standardization fails, fall back to the original molecule. Use the standardized molecules for all features. Then replace the single pseudo-Huber XGBoost with the average of two XGBoosts: the existing pseudo-Huber one and a squared-error one (max_depth 5, other settings the same, random_state seed+1). Leave the MLP members and the 0.4/0.3/0.3 weights unchanged, so the tree half is the mean of the two XGBoosts.
backlog.title: Neutralize + second squared-error XGBoost

backlog.spec: For test molecules, build features from K=5 molecule copies with randomized atom order. Use Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True) with the seed set via random.seed/np.random, then re-parse. Compute descriptors and Morgan counts for each copy, run them through the already-trained MLPs, and average the predictions. The Morgan features hardly change with atom order, but some descriptors (for example Ipc and BCUT) can differ, so this smooths descriptor noise. Leave XGBoost on canonical features. Keep the featurization cost small by caching.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation for the MLPs

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out 15% of the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold. Train the three members on the remaining rows and fit non-negative blend weights on the holdout by scipy nnls, normalized to sum to 1. Clip each weight to [0.15, 0.6]. Then refit all members on the full training data and apply those weights. To fit the weights, use a cheaper MLP ensemble (2 nets per member). Weights learned per fold adapt to the data instead of staying fixed at 0.4/0.3/0.3.
backlog.title: Blend weight retune via inner holdout

backlog.spec: Add a fourth blend member. Build a feature matrix of quantile-transformed descriptors plus log1p Morgan counts (kept columns). Apply a RandomFourier feature map (sklearn.kernel_approximation.RBFSampler, gamma about 1/n_features, 3000 components, random_state=seed) and fit RidgeCV (alphas 1 to 100). Blend with weight 0.15 and scale the other weights by 0.85. This is a smooth kernel model that differs from trees and MLPs.
backlog.title: Wide random-feature ridge/kernel member

backlog.spec: Append to the XGBoost input only (not the MLPs) the following: 512-bit Morgan count fingerprints at radius 3 with chirality off, plus counts of fragment functional groups from rdkit.Chem.Fragments (all fr_* functions). Lower colsample_bytree to 0.3 to compensate for the larger matrix. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Pooled radius-3 Morgan and ring-fragment counts for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace each descriptor-MLP fit with 3 sequential snapshots. Use MLPRegressor with warm_start=True, max_iter=60, solver adam, and learning_rate_init reset to 1e-3, 5e-4 and 2.5e-4 before each phase (set via the estimator's learning_rate_init attribute). Disable early_stopping, since sklearn warm_start with early stopping is fiddly. Average the predictions of the three snapshots. Use 5 seeds and the same alpha. Keep the Morgan MLP unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot-ensembled MLPs with warm restarts

backlog.spec: Train the two MLP members on winsorized targets. Clip y to the 1st and 99th percentile of the training targets, and centre and scale it. Predict, then invert the scaling. This is a robust-loss proxy for the MLP half only, and XGBoost keeps the raw y. The MLPs are rather sensitive to outlying logD values because they use squared error.
backlog.title: Huber-clipped target for MLPs

backlog.spec: For the log1p-Morgan MLP, augment the training set 3x. Each copy randomly zeroes 10% of the nonzero fingerprint entries (seeded) and adds Gaussian noise of sd 0.1 to the quantile descriptors. Keep the labels. Train as before on the stacked 3N rows, and use a smaller max_iter if runtime is an issue. This acts as dropout regularization, which sklearn's MLP lacks.
backlog.title: Dropout-like input noise augmentation on the MLP fingerprint member

backlog.spec: After blending, compute a correction. For each test molecule find its 5 nearest training neighbours by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan counts (MinMax). Take the neighbours' out-of-fold residuals, from 5-fold inner CV of the cheap XGBoost only, weight them by similarity cubed, and add 0.5 times the weighted mean residual, applied only when the maximum similarity is above 0.6. Otherwise add nothing. This local correction exploits series of analogues.
backlog.title: Pair-difference (Siamese-style) k-NN residual correction

backlog.spec: In featurize, keep the largest fragment of each molecule and neutralize it with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger before computing Morgan counts, descriptors and SMARTS counts. Compute the formal charge on the original molecule so the ionization signal is kept. In fit_predict, make p_tree the average of the existing pseudo-Huber XGBRegressor and a second XGBRegressor with objective reg:squarederror, max_depth 5 and random_state seed+1. Leave the MLP members and the 0.4/0.3/0.3 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Neutralize plus second squared-error XGBoost

backlog.spec: For the two MLP members only, build the test features from the canonical molecule plus 4 variants made with Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True, canonical=False), then re-parse each. Morgan counts are order-invariant, so this only matters if you also add small perturbations. To make it useful, perturb the training set instead. Duplicate each training molecule once with Morgan counts computed using a random bond-order-invariant atom ordering and additive noise on the log1p count features (Gaussian, sd 0.05) for the fingerprint MLP. Average predictions over the original and noisy test copies. Keep the XGBoost member untouched.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation for MLPs

backlog.spec: Replace the sklearn MLPRegressor on descriptors with a small numpy or sklearn partial_fit loop. Use solver='adam' with warm restarts: for 4 cycles of 40 epochs, set learning_rate_init manually per epoch via cosine decay from 2e-3 to 1e-5 (MLPRegressor with warm_start=True, max_iter=1, and the optimizer's learning_rate_init attribute updated each epoch). Average predictions from the end of each cycle. Use 3 seeds. Keep the blend weights.
backlog.title: Cosine-annealed SGD MLP snapshot ensemble

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out 15% of the training rows, grouped by Murcko scaffold, and fit the three members on the remaining 85% with fewer seeds. Find the nonnegative weights summing to 1 that minimize MAE on the holdout, using a coarse grid with step 0.1. Then refit all members on the full training set and blend with the shrunk weights 0.5*learned + 0.5*[0.4,0.3,0.3]. Reuse the cached features to save time.
backlog.title: Blend weight retune with inner holdout

backlog.spec: Train both MLP members on y_hat = the XGBoost out-of-fold predictions' residual sign-compressed: first compute 5-fold OOF pseudo-Huber XGBoost predictions with a light config (300 trees, depth 5). Train the MLPs to predict y minus 0.5*oof, and add 0.5*the test XGBoost prediction back at inference. This is partial residualization. Keep the blend weights.
backlog.title: Quantile (median) MLP via L1-friendly target

backlog.spec: For the fingerprint MLP, use log1p counts of two Morgan generators, radius 1 with 1024 bits and radius 3 with 2048 bits, concatenated and filtered to columns with at least 10 nonzero training molecules. Add the quantile-normalized descriptors as before. Use hidden sizes (512,128) and alpha 0.1 with 4 seeds.
backlog.title: Wide Morgan MLP with multi-radius count input

backlog.spec: For both MLP members, augment the training set with 1x as many mixup samples. Pick random pairs of training rows (seeded RandomState), draw lambda from Beta(0.4,0.4), and mix both features and targets linearly. Train the MLPs on the original rows plus the mixed rows. Because the rows double, reduce each ensemble by one seed to stay within the time limit.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation for MLPs

backlog.spec: Add features that mimic a message-passing network. For each molecule, compute per-atom Crippen logP contributions and Gasteiger charges. Then pool the sums over each atom's 1-hop and 2-hop neighbourhoods using the adjacency matrix and its square. Aggregate the results with sum, max and min over atoms, giving about 12 extra columns. Append them to the descriptors for XGBoost and the MLPs.
backlog.title: Atom-environment pooled GNN-like features

backlog.spec: Add a second XGBRegressor with booster='dart', rate_drop 0.1, skip_drop 0.5, 400 trees, lr 0.06, max_depth 6, colsample_bytree 0.3 and pseudo-Huber loss. Average its predictions with the existing XGBoost to form p_tree. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Dart boosting second XGBoost member

backlog.spec: Wrap the three members in a bagging loop. Use 3 bags, each trained on a random 80% of the training Murcko scaffold groups, drawn with the seed. Average the blended predictions of the bags. Cut the ensemble sizes to 3 MLP seeds for the descriptor MLP and 2 for the fingerprint MLP, and use 500 XGBoost trees at lr 0.045 to stay under 10 minutes. Cache the features across bags.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of the whole blend

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, for the test set only, build K=8 additional versions of each test molecule using Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True) with RDKit random state seeded from seed, re-parse them, and compute the Morgan counts and descriptors. Predict with the two MLP members on each version (using the same quantile transformer and keep mask) and average with the canonical prediction. Leave XGBoost as is. Note that Morgan counts and most descriptors are invariant to atom order, so if the features turn out identical, instead augment by adding Gaussian noise (sd 0.1 in quantile space) to the MLP test inputs and average 8 draws.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: For the descriptor MLP, replace the 5 independently seeded nets with 3 nets. Each net uses warm_start=True and max_iter=40 with learning_rate_init 1e-3, and is fitted 4 times in a row with early_stopping=False. Before each refit, reset learning_rate_init to 1e-3 to simulate a restart. Collect predictions after every cycle and average all snapshots. Keep the fingerprint MLP unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot-ensembled MLPs via warm restarts

backlog.spec: For both MLP members, build an augmented training set. Draw 1x extra samples by picking random pairs (i,j) from the training set with RandomState(seed), lambda~Beta(0.4,0.4), and form x=lam*xi+(1-lam)*xj and y=lam*yi+(1-lam)*yj on the transformed inputs. Restrict pairs to j among the 10 nearest neighbours of i in the quantile-descriptor space, to keep the mixes meaningful. Train the MLPs on the original data plus the mixed samples. Keep XGBoost unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation for the MLPs

backlog.spec: Replace the single XGBoost fit with 6 fits. Each fit trains on a random 80% of the Murcko scaffold groups of the training set, drawn with RandomState(seed+k). Use 500 trees and lr 0.04, and keep the other parameters. Average the 6 predictions. Compute scaffolds with MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of the XGBoost member

backlog.spec: Add GNN-like pooled features for XGBoost and the descriptor MLP. For each atom compute a vector of [Crippen logP contribution, Crippen MR contribution, TPSA contribution, Gasteiger charge, degree, aromatic flag]. Then run 2 rounds of neighbour averaging over the molecular graph, and pool each round over all atoms by sum, max and min. Append the resulting features (6 features x 3 rounds x 3 pools) to the descriptor block. Replace NaN with 0.
backlog.title: Pooled neighbourhood graph features

backlog.spec: For both MLP members, fit once, compute training residuals, and then refit using sample_weight (supported by MLPRegressor in sklearn >=1.7; otherwise emulate it by duplicating rows with a residual below 1.0 once, and others zero or once). Use Huber weights w=min(1,1.0/|r|) rounded into integer row-duplication counts. Average the refit with the first fit for each seed.
backlog.title: Huber-loss MLP via a PyTorch-free IRLS reweighting

backlog.spec: Add a second tree member. Use XGBRegressor with booster gbtree, colsample_bynode=0.2, colsample_bytree=0.7, max_depth=8, min_child_weight=5, learning_rate 0.03, 600 trees, subsample 0.6, reg_lambda 5, objective reg:absoluteerror, and random_state seed+7. Average it with the existing XGBoost prediction to form p_tree. Keep the blend weights the same.
backlog.title: Wide random-subspace XGBoost with extra-randomized splits

backlog.spec: Add continuous ionization-state features for pH 7.4. For each molecule compute a crude acid pKa class (carboxylic acid ~4, tetrazole ~4.5, acyl sulfonamide ~4.5, phenol ~10, sulfonamide ~10) and a base pKa class (aliphatic amine ~9.5, amidine ~12, pyridine ~5, imidazole ~7, aniline ~4.5). Use SMARTS for these, and take the fraction ionized for the strongest acid and the strongest base from Henderson-Hasselbalch. Also add the net expected charge. Append the 3 columns to the ion block, so they reach XGBoost and the descriptor MLP.
backlog.title: Target-aware fingerprint input via logD-pH ionization class features

cand.description: Mixup augmentation (1x extra samples, Beta(0.4,0.4), partners from 10 nearest neighbours in quantile-descriptor space) for both MLP members.

incumbent.description: Add a third blend member: MLP on log1p Morgan counts (columns with >=10 nonzero training molecules) plus quantile-transformed descriptors, 3 seeds, blended 0.4 XGB / 0.3 descriptor MLP / 0.3 this MLP.

last_tail: the job did not finish within 600 s
memo: Helped: model swaps and blending. RF to LightGBM (0.7230 to 0.5976), descriptors (0.5447), SMARTS ionization counts (0.5340/0.5347), XGBoost (0.5182), the 50/50 MLP blend (0.5029), then a third member, an MLP on log1p Morgan counts. That third member is the incumbent (0.4913/0.4944). Did not help: ExtraTrees, descriptors-only, MACCS, atom-pair/torsion, larger fingerprints, feature pruning, Huber tweaks, CatBoost, scaffold weights (0.4946), stacking, shallower XGBoost, median blending (0.4947), outlier dropping (0.4929). Runtime-cutting variants were worse (0.5124 to 0.5247). Several larger setups crashed, so keep jobs well under 10 minutes. Near-misses: fragment neutralization (0.4892), second XGBoost (0.4911), extra descriptors (0.4914), RidgeCV member (0.4872/0.4900). Gains are now near the 0.0042 noise. Next: combine neutralization with the second XGBoost, then tune blend weights and MLP dropout/width. Replicate promising runs. Don't repeat tried ideas, since they only produce aborts.
